items.title: Camden County Water District Gets $223K For Drinking Water Upgrades
items.desc: CAMDEN COUNTY, Mo. — Camden County Public Water Supply District No. 5 has received a $223,000 interest-free loan from the Missouri Department of Natural Resources to help plan and design future drinking water system improvements.
items.body: CAMDEN COUNTY, Mo. — Camden County Public Water Supply District No. 5 has received a $223,000 interest-free loan from the Missouri Department of Natural Resources to help plan and design future drinking water system improvements. The funding comes through the department’s Planning and Design Loan Program and will cover early engineering and administrative costs while the district works toward a larger construction funding package. The district estimates the full improvement project will cost about $3 million, with construction expected to begin in 2028. According to DNR, the planning loan carries no interest and has a five-year term. The department estimates that will save local ratepayers about $48,000 in interest compared with other financing options. “Investing in local water infrastructure is not just about improving drinking water systems; it’s about revitalizing communities and ensuring residents have access to abundant, safe drinking water,” said Jake Buxton, director of the Missouri Department of Natural Resources. The larger project could eventually qualify for additional financing through Missouri’s Drinking Water State Revolving Fund, which supports improvements to water treatment plants, distribution systems, water storage, supply facilities, and other drinking water infrastructure. DNR said the Camden County project will be funded wholly or in part with money received from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. More information about Missouri drinking water and wastewater funding programs is available through the Department of Natural Resources’ State Revolving Fund program.

items.title: Osage Beach's Hwy 42 Sidewalk Is Switching Sides... And Now It Might Actually Get Done
items.desc: How hard is it to build a sidewalk?
items.body: How hard is it to build a sidewalk? Expert-level hard, if you're the City of Osage Beach, you want to build it along Highway 42, and you're using government grants to get it done. The City is more than four years in, on a project to build an .85-mile sidewalk along Highway 42 using federal TAP Grant money... and they haven't even broken ground. But a huge change to the project could result in it finally being started — and completed — in 2027. The sidewalk was originally set to run along the east side of the highway, connecting the Prewitt's Point Shopping Center (which ends at Lowe's) to the City Park and then to School of the Osage High School. They're moving the ENTIRE sidewalk across Hwy 42. Yep. The OTHER SIDE of the highway. And now it might FINALLY get built in 2027. But the obstacles were legion. The topography of the area meant more construction cost. And some property owners along the path were reticent to work with the City on easements. "Not everybody was eager about the project," said Project Manager Colten Wright. The City was determined to find a way. It had already paid engineers for a design; and more importantly, the federal Transportation Alternatives Program (TAP) grant cost-share had already been applied for and approved. That grant would cover 75% of the project. Wright explained, "If you don’t carry through on a TAP project, the likelihood of you getting a TAP project again is very slim." So if the City decided to punt on the sidewalk, he said it would almost certainly affect its chances of getting federal funds to help build other sidewalks or other alternative transportation infrastructure in the future. items.title: Marshfield Community Theatre Presents: Carrie: The Musical This Halloween
items.desc: This Halloween season, the Marshfield Community Theatre is bringing you something old and something new. “We are currently producing Carrie: The Musical, based on the iconic story by Stephen King,” […]
items.body: This Halloween season, the Marshfield Community Theatre is bringing you something old and something new. “We are currently producing Carrie: The Musical, based on the iconic story by Stephen King,” shared an excited Kelby Lorenz, Director of Carrie and Director of Outreach for Marshfield Community Theatre. “We chose this show because it’s October; we are doing it Halloween weekend. It seemed like a really good spooky show, but when I read the script, it tells a really incredible story,” reflected Lorenz. “One of the things that I love about this show and the way that it’s interpreted is that it’s a closed loop-we end where we start. We got to really play with the idea of how long have we been stuck in this loop…and how long have we been trying to stop the destruction.” “It’s a cool concept to play with-around the idea of trauma, how it stays with us…and how traumatic moments can really impact the way we interact with each other,” expressed Lorenz. “It really centers on that theme-what does it cost to be kind?” The cast includes around 16, with most actors new to MCT, including a mix of MSU students and brand-new actors. The production team includes Lorenz as Director, Nico Jenkins as Assistant Director, Linley Wilson as Music Director, Miliani Kloster as Choreographer, and Toni Lorenz as Production Manager. “It’s been super fun,” shared Lauren Knight, a Missouri State student playing Carrie White. “I haven’t done a lot of roles where I’m a lead- it’s been a bit of a change. It’s been fun to get to know this character. She’s been a bit of a challenge…I’ve learned to be more vulnerable on stage. items.title: Athlete of the Week: Johnny Carriger, Crocker Soccer
items.desc: Share on Facebook Share on Twitter As an underclassman, Johnny Carriger was ready for the moment, scoring a hat trick in Crocker’s district championship game. “I think we just wanted it more,” Johnny said. “They came out
items.body: As an underclassman, Johnny Carriger was ready for the moment, scoring a hat trick in Crocker’s district championship game. “I think we just wanted it more,” Johnny said. “They came out like they were going to win. They went up 2-0 in the first half, and I was like someone’s got to step up. So I did.” It was his second hat trick of the tournament, all while battling illness and injury. “He had a 103 fever at district time to send us to the final,” said Crocker Head Soccer Coach Rich Heenan. “Two weeks prior he had broke his hand and powered through without anything on his hand. [Johnny] played the rest of the season in a full cast.” On top of toughness, scoring goals runs in the family. His older brother, Tristen, put up Laquey’s lone goal in the Hornet’s state semifinal game. Johnny was there watching in the stands. “Whenever he scored it I was like dang, why couldn’t that be me,” Johnny said. Now, Tristen is Crocker’s assistant soccer coach. “I just cannot call him coach,” Johnny said. “It’s just too funny.” “He’s watched me play for years,” Tristen Carriger said. “But now it’s me watching him play.” Johnny is nearing 100 career goals as a varsity starter. 34 of them are in the last 16 games. Tristen gets a front-row view of his brother’s success and more. “He likes to help his teammates and help them figure out how to pass the ball better [or] how to do a soccer move,” Tristen said. “[He] even leads them to getting their first goal.” Johnny has no plans of slowing his scoring spree, but as his brother would wan, he’s turned into a leader on top of a striker.

items.title: Sunshine Club learns history at October meeting
items.desc: The Fair Grove Sunshine Club met October 14th at the Fair Grove Senior Center. The members attending were Evelyn Kerby, Marilyn Smith, Robbie Gillet, Holly Barlow, Lynda Hutchison, Carolyn Riggi, […]
items.body: The Fair Grove Sunshine Club met October 14th at the Fair Grove Senior Center. The members attending were Evelyn Kerby, Marilyn Smith, Robbie Gillet, Holly Barlow, Lynda Hutchison, Carolyn Riggi, Mary Terry, Peggy Schletty, Rue Withers, Toni Woffard, Ellen Carter, Pam Meyers & Carol Highfill. Everyone had lunch and the Business Meeting followed. Marilyn Smith gave the History of the Sunshine Club. It was started as the W.P.F.A Club in 1923 which stands for the Women’s Progressive Farmer’s Association. When it disbanded in 1986, the Club wanted to continue on, so it was named the Sunshine Club. The Club has met every month for 103 years. The Club has met in everyone’s homes, and went to many interesting places all over the area. We have toured many educational places and always looked forward to the good meals we have shared in homes, Tea Rooms, Restaurants, and the Senior Center. New members are always welcomed.

items.body: Warm up with a delicious meal and support a great cause! The community is invited to the CWF’s Chili & Soup Luncheon on Wednesday, November 4th from 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM. The event will be held at the Buffalo First Christian Church, located at 502 N. Maple St., Buffalo, MO. In addition to a variety of hot chilis and soups, attendees can browse a homemade bake sale and enjoy a beautiful quilt show showcasing local talent. Admission is by donation only, and carry-out options are available for those on the go. Come out for great food, beautiful quilts, and wonderful community fellowship!
